questions.text: Which Article most directly concerns equality before law and equal protection of laws?
Which institution administers elections to Parliament and State Legislatures?
Who ordinarily leads the Union Council of Ministers?
A case concerns life and personal liberty rather than equality or civic duties. Which provision is most directly relevant?
Which institution is the closest match for urban local civic services?
Which distinction between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is most accurate?
options: Rights protect specified legal interests; Directive Principles guide governance and policy
Fundamental Rights apply only to municipalities

questions.text: A law restricts a freedom associated with Article 19. Which conclusion is most careful?
options: Any restriction automatically violates the Constitution
A restriction is valid merely because a law exists
Assess the applicable constitutional grounds and requirements; enactment alone does not settle validity

questions.text: Both national and state election bodies conduct elections. Which distinction is correct?
options: The national body directly conducts every municipal election
The state body administers Lok Sabha elections
Their roles differ: national elections to Parliament/State Legislatures versus local-body elections under State Election Commissions

questions.text: Parliament has amendment power. What important limitation does the basic-structure doctrine establish?
options: An amendment cannot destroy the Constitution's basic structure
No constitutional provision can ever be amended
Only municipalities may amend the Constitution
Every amendment needs approval from every district

questions.text: A citizen says a policy is unfair but identifies no right or legal standard. What is the best first step in analysis?
options: Assume every unpopular policy is unconstitutional
Identify relevant provisions, facts and the applicable legal test before concluding
Use Fundamental Duties instead of evidence
Conclude judicial review never applies to policy
